subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The Fraud Triangle
description: A quick, practical guide to The Fraud Triangle.

hook.text: A trusted employee steals $2 million over five years. Nobody suspected a thing.

buildup.text: The fraud triangle explains why people cheat: pressure (need money), opportunity (weak controls), and rationalization.

discovery.text: Most fraudsters are first-time offenders. They look exactly like your most reliable employee.

twist.text: Companies focus on hiring honest people. The fraud triangle shows that circumstances create dishonesty.

climax.text: Remove any leg of the triangle — pressure, opportunity, or rationalization — and fraud becomes less likely.

punchline.text: Pressure. Opportunity. Rationalization. That's how fraud starts.

quiz.question: What are the three elements of the fraud triangle?
